title: The Stages of Mitosis
prompt: Put the stages of mitosis in order, from the first to the last.
learning_objective: Order the stages of mitosis and describe what the chromosomes are doing at each one.
reference: Cell cycle and mitosis, GCSE/A-level biology sequencing activity

spec.title: The Stages of Mitosis
spec.instruction: Drag the five stages from the shuffled column into the order a cell passes through them, then press Check.
spec.prompt: Put the stages of mitosis in order, from the first to the last.
spec.why: Mitosis is one continuous process; its stages are named for what the chromosomes are doing at each moment.

items.note: Chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes and the spindle begins to form.
Chromosomes line up single file along the cell's equator, attached to spindle fibres.
Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles of the cell.
Two nuclear envelopes re-form, one around each set of chromosomes.
The cytoplasm divides, producing two genetically identical daughter cells.

title: Linear Search, Step by Step
prompt: In what order does a linear search work through a list?
learning_objective: Trace the steps of a linear search and explain why its cost grows with the length of the list.
reference: Linear and binary search, KS4/AP Computer Science algorithms

spec.title: Linear Search, Step by Step
spec.instruction: The steps of a linear search are shuffled. Drag them into the order the computer carries them out, then press Check.
spec.prompt: In what order does a linear search work through a list?
spec.why: A linear search checks items one at a time from one end, so its cost grows in step with the length of the list.

items.text: Start at the first item in the list.
items.note: A linear search always begins at one end and moves through in order.

items.text: Compare the current item with the target.
items.note: Each item is tested once, against the value being searched for.

items.text: If it matches, stop and report the position.
items.note: A match ends the search early - there is no need to look any further.

items.text: If not, move on to the next item.
items.note: A miss advances the search by exactly one position.

items.text: Repeat until found or the list ends.
items.note: This repetition is what makes it an algorithm rather than a single comparison.

items.text: If the list ends, report no match.
items.note: Reaching the end without a match is the other way the algorithm can finish.

title: Quantities and Their SI Units
prompt: Match each physical quantity to its SI unit.
learning_objective: Match physical quantities to their SI units and recognise the base units those units are built from.
reference: Dimensional analysis, SI base units (A-level physics)

spec.title: Quantities and Their SI Units
spec.instruction: Select a quantity on the left, then its SI unit on the right. Correct pairs lock in; wrong ones bounce back.
spec.prompt: Match each physical quantity to its SI unit.

pairs.note: One newton accelerates one kilogram at one metre per second squared.
A joule is a newton-metre: a force acting through a distance.
A watt is one joule per second.
One coulomb is the charge carried by one ampere for one second.
A volt is one joule per coulomb.
An ohm is one volt per ampere.
